sentences.text: The only known species of this dinosaur is H. australis, a name combining the Mapudungun word for duck with the Greek word for lizard to reflect its southern location.
Originally described in 1984 as a species of Kritosaurus, Huallasaurus was recognized as a distinct genus separate from Secernosaurus and other Kritosaurini members in a 2022 study.

CT scans revealed that Huallasaurus vertebrae had a relatively dense trabecular architecture and lacked invasive pneumaticity in the centra, neural arches, and neural spines, making the internal vertebral structure more similar to silesaurs like Silesaurus than to other archosauriforms.
The lack of invasive air sacs in Huallasaurus vertebrae supports the hypothesis that air sac diverticula did not evolve in Ornithischia and suggests a "pelvic bellows" ventilation mechanism.
Huallasaurus may have supported its large body size and fat reserves through a combination of dense trabecular bone, thin cortical walls, and the absence of invasive air sacs.
While Huallasaurus vertebrae superficially resemble those of large mammals with expanded trabecular matrices and thin walls, the functional equivalence of these structures is speculative.

Rozadilla et al. (2022) recovered Huallasaurus within a clade consisting entirely of South American saurolophines, which was named Austrokritosauria and is recovered as the sister taxon to Kritosaurini.
Huallasaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately between 73 and 69 million years ago, specifically within the Maastrichtian stage from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
It is currently debated whether the similarity in vertebral structure between Huallasaurus and silesaurs indicates a deep phylogenetic relationship or convergent evolution.
